trigger: consume_ticket leaves status='approved' and nothing prunes, so the 'approved' bucket grows without bound; ScheduleRunner issues 3 query() calls per tick, each now taking mtx_
summary: The new lock on query() couples an unbounded status-bucket scan to the security-critical consume path; measured 112ms at 1M rows
classification_rationale: measured latency on a serialised path shared with a one-time-capability redemption, not a style question

trigger: read the #2443 changelog fragment against mcp_server.cpp:3242, which still uses the two-argument overload
summary: Fragment claimed tickets can no longer be burned by drift; no caller passes a precondition, so nothing is protected
classification_rationale: a released changelog is read as a record of protection in force; FALSE ASSURANCE, not wording

trigger: an operator imports or authors a definition whose id starts mcp., producing a denial string absent from an enumerated SIEM-keying token list
summary: New denial string missing from the documented stable-token list for instruction.import denials
classification_rationale: the list is a published SIEM contract, so an omission conceals a security-relevant denial

trigger: upgrade with an existing mcp.-prefixed definition, then re-import or reinstall it
summary: The reservation is a breaking change to instruction authoring and no artifact called it breaking; no upgrade note existed
classification_rationale: omission conceals a breaking change, which is the named I7 raise

trigger: author YAML with metadata.id under the reserved prefix: Validate returns green, Save returns 400
summary: The YAML validator mirrors the store's id gate byte-for-byte by design; the new rule landed only in the store, breaking validate-implies-save for the third time (#1993, #2010)
classification_rationale: the file's own comment states the contract; copying rather than sharing the gate is what broke it each time

trigger: sqlite3 prepare or step failure during the pre-consume read
summary: A failed read was classified kNotConsumable, telling the operator a live human-approved ticket was spent
classification_rationale: E6 caps it today because no production caller passes a precondition; it becomes HIGH the moment one does

summary: Approval ids are bearer capabilities by this file's own comment and were logged in full at four sites
classification_rationale: fixed at the sink rather than the one new instance

trigger: a SIEM rule keyed on either reserved-prefix denial
summary: One rule emitted two different denial wordings with no shared token
classification_rationale: resolved together with UP-3 by extracting one predicate and one message

trigger: a future precondition author reads the header and puts an RBAC check in the callback
summary: The header named RBAC as precondition subject matter, which would place authority outside the core approval gate
classification_rationale: ADR-1005 routed row: one core-owned approval primitive

summary: A throwing caller callback escaped the store method onto an httplib worker, and was untested

trigger: a forward wall-clock jump during a submit(), expiring every pending and approved-unconsumed ticket in one pass
summary: The expiry sweep is an unguarded wall-clock bulk pass with no probe-by-outcome, persisted anchor, or cap
classification_rationale: ADJUDICATED DOWN from the agent's BLOCKING: the mass-invalidation hazard is entirely pre-existing and unchanged by this diff, which alters only the latency coupling; that half is fixed by the v6 indexes. Filed against #2508 rather than fixed here.

trigger: an operator runs the detection command in the new upgrade note before upgrading
summary: The upgrade note's curl command called a route that does not exist; both reviewers' proposed corrections truncate at 100 definitions while shipped content is 230, so any API-based check can report a false all-clear
classification_rationale: harmful guidance: the command silently reports no affected content, the opposite of the note's purpose. Both corrections adjudicated wrong and replaced with a direct database query.

trigger: open a pre-existing mcp.-prefixed definition in the dashboard YAML editor and save it
summary: 'Stays editable' was false: validate_yaml_source runs before the create/update fork, so the YAML editor refuses to save such a definition
classification_rationale: the store rule is create-only but the validator is not; the claim is corrected rather than the check loosened, and the exception is now stated in all three places

trigger: any regression reinstating a lock-held precondition, which is exactly what the test exists to catch
summary: A joinable std::thread was destroyed during the assertion's unwind, so the guarded regression aborted the whole test binary instead of failing one test
classification_rationale: derived LOW (E6: test binary only) but gates as an ownership policy floor; reproduced by two reviewers and re-verified after the fix

trigger: read the claim that product-pack install refuses the prefix against workflow_routes.cpp
summary: Product-pack install was listed as refusing with a 400; it never carries a declared id through, so the branch is unreachable from there
classification_rationale: the security property holds by a different mechanism than the one documented; consistency-auditor asserted the opposite and was adjudicated wrong against the code

summary: The caught exception's what() was placed into a message the adjacent header documents as reaching the MCP envelope, which must carry no caller-derived text

trigger: read consume_ticket's doc block against the ConsumePrecondition block four lines away
summary: The round-1 fix corrected one site naming RBAC as precondition subject matter and left the sibling, which then contradicted the new paragraph
classification_rationale: the round-1 commit claimed this was fixed; it fixed the instance, not the file

trigger: none: the store-failure branch of get_checked had no regression test
summary: The behaviour the round-1 fix was about shipped with no test for its own core branch; the reviewer proved it was cheap to provoke
